pr.title: mir-opt: Use one MirPatch in MatchBranchSimplification
pr.author: dianqk

processing.reason: The PR is an internal compiler refactor whose only behavioral claim is patch lifetime/application timing: it replaces a per-block `MirPatch` (created and applied while iterating candidates) with one `MirPatch` created before the loop and applied once afterward. The frozen analysis itself states this is "not a claim that the rewritten match semantics themselves changed," and the source confirms the old and new code perform the same simplifications. An earlier per-block patch only rewrites the current SwitchInt block's terminator and appends new blocks/statements; it does not change later candidate blocks' terminators or their target blocks' contents, so later `can_simplify` decisions are the same. Any resulting MIR differences are block ordering/local allocation, not runtime values. Therefore there is no source-grounded program pair whose original and transformed executions produce different defined values; constructing one would require inventing an unrelated semantic difference not justified by PR 140080.

analysis.summary: Refactors MatchBranchSimplification from applying a fresh MirPatch inside each per-block simplification (while iterating block indices) to creating one MirPatch for the whole body, threading it through SimplifyMatch::simplify, and applying it once before CFG cleanup. The reusable concern is patch lifetime/application timing: all candidate SwitchInt blocks should be analyzed against one coherent MIR snapshot, then their edits applied atomically, rather than mutating the body between block visits.
analysis.originalLogic: In run_pass, iterate body.basic_blocks.indices(), select blocks whose terminator is SwitchInt with Operand::Copy or Operand::Move discriminator and whose targets do not contain the block itself, then call SimplifyToIf::simplify and SimplifyToExp::simplify with &mut Body. Each successful simplify call creates its own MirPatch::new(body) internally, adds StorageLive/assignment/new statements/StorageDead, replaces the terminator, and calls patch.apply(body) immediately. A should_cleanup flag is set, and after the loop simplify_cfg(tcx, body) runs if any simplification occurred.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical transformation applied a separate MirPatch per candidate block immediately during iteration over body.basic_blocks.indices(), so later candidate blocks were visited in a body already modified by earlier patches. The corrected transformation instead creates one MirPatch::new(body) before the loop, passes &mut MirPatch and an immutable &Body into simplify, accumulates all per-block edits in that single patch, and calls patch.apply(body) once after the loop (only when apply_patch is true) before simplify_cfg. This is a patch-batching/timing change, not a claim that the rewritten match semantics themselves changed.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies containing one or more basic blocks with a SwitchInt terminator whose discriminator is Operand::Copy or Operand::Move and whose targets do not include that block. The distinguishing cases have multiple such candidate blocks in the same body, especially where an earlier simplification inserts/retargets blocks that a later candidate or its target set would observe if patches were applied between iterations.
analysis.trigger: MatchBranchSimplification visits more than one simplifyable SwitchInt block in a body, or a simplifyable block whose surrounding MIR is affected by an earlier per-block patch applied during the same pass.
preconditions: The block terminator is SwitchInt with discr Operand::Copy(_) or Operand::Move(_).
targets.all_targets() does not contain the switch block itself.
can_simplify succeeds for the targets, typing environment, branch blocks, and discriminator type.
At least one SimplifyToIf or SimplifyToExp simplification succeeds so apply_patch becomes true.
pitfalls: Creating MirPatch::new(body) inside each simplify call means each patch is based on a body that may already contain earlier patches; a single patch should be created from the original body.
Applying a patch while iterating body.basic_blocks.indices() mutates the body between candidate visits and can make later analysis observe inserted or rewritten blocks.

Deferring edits requires threading the same MirPatch through simplify and applying it exactly once; forgetting patch.apply(body) would leave the accumulated statements and terminator replacement unapplied.
simplify_cfg must still run after patch.apply when apply_patch is true; applying the patch without cleanup changes the scheduling of CFG simplification.
Do not conflate this patch-timing change with general borrowing or post-copy overwrite concerns; the supplied patch contains no such test-layer evidence.
analysis.testStrategy: Construct a MIR body with at least two simplifyable SwitchInt blocks and run MatchBranchSimplification once. Verify every candidate is simplified against the same pre-pass body snapshot, the accumulated MirPatch is applied exactly once, and simplify_cfg runs afterward. Add focused MIR tests covering multiple candidates plus the exclusion guards: a SwitchInt targeting its own block must not be simplified, and both Operand::Copy and Operand::Move discriminators must be handled. Compare decoded MIR before and after; this PR itself adds no regression test, so the test should target the multi-candidate patch-batching condition rather than rely on an existing expectation.
